summary: Package initialiser whose only job is to import the local, s3, http and sftp backend subpackages so their @register_storage_backend decorators populate the backend registry. The registry's ensure_backends_loaded() imports this package lazily before any lookup or registration. Verified support matrix at 8a979e2 (isinstance against runtime_checkable protocols): local = Read, Write, Enumerate, Delete, Metadata, Copy, Directory (no RangedRead; facade uses native seekable handle); s3 family = Read, Write, Enumerate, Delete, Metadata, Copy, RangedRead (no Directory); sftp = Read, Write, Enumerate, Delete, Metadata, Directory, RangedRead (no Copy); http = Read, Write, Metadata, RangedRead (no Enumerate, Delete, Copy, Directory).
extension_points: New built-in backend: add a subpackage under storage/backends/, decorate the composed class with @register_storage_backend(CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE.X), and add an import line here.
Third-party backends do not need to edit this file: register_storage_backend calls ensure_backends_loaded() first, so a caller registration made after import overrides the built-in one.
lifecycle_notes: Imported lazily by storage/registry/registry.py ensure_backends_loaded() (cached by sys.modules), not by the package root.
Every backend subpackage must import on a base install (typing-extensions only); SDK and [http]-stack imports are deferred into functions and enforced by tests/test_slim_install.py.
documentation_hooks: Backend support matrix page (Read/Write/Enumerate/Delete/Metadata/Copy/Directory/RangedRead per provider) generated from or checked against get_registered_backends().
Contributor guide: adding a storage backend (registration, import-on-base-install rule, conformance tests to extend).
Architecture: registry population order and override semantics.
examples: examples/capability_checks/example.py — compares capabilities of the registered local and HTTP backends through StorageFacade.supports()
risks: AGENTS.md storage section is stale: it says local supports 'all but enumerate' and sftp 'read/write/delete/metadata/directory', but code, README.md matrix and tests/storage/protocols/test_backend_conformance.py show local and sftp both implement StorageEnumerateProtocol.

`import mountainash_transport.storage.backends as b` raises ImportError ('cannot import name backends from storage') because the package root rebinds the name `storage` to the storage() factory function; `from mountainash_transport.storage.backends import X` and plain `import ...` work (verified at 8a979e2).
open_questions: Should the support matrix gain a RangedRead column? README.md 'Supported storage' omits RangedReadProtocol although http, s3 and sftp implement it and docs/read-access-modes.md depends on it.

evidence.detail: Only content is four `from . import <backend>` lines with noqa F401 for registration side effects.
ensure_backends_loaded() imports mountainash_transport.storage.backends; register_storage_backend calls it before inserting into _backend_registry.
EXPECTED_PROTOCOLS lists StorageEnumerateProtocol for LOCAL and excludes only StorageCopyProtocol for SFTP, contradicting AGENTS.md.
Supported storage table: Local all columns; S3 family no Directories; SFTP no Copy; HTTP Read/Write/Metadata only; no RangedRead column.
Storage > Backends bullet lists local as 'all but enumerate' and sftp without enumerate (stale).
